properties.text: For all blocks received via P2P, if len(rlp.encode(block)) > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (EIP-7934, ~8MB), the block MUST be rejected before any further processing (header validation, transaction execution, or state modification) occurs.

reachability.notes: Any P2P peer can send an arbitrarily large block payload. The size check must occur before RLP decoding to prevent memory exhaustion. This is a Fusaka-specific defense (EIP-7934).

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE allows oversized blocks to cause memory exhaustion or excessive CPU usage on receiving nodes, potentially crashing validators and disrupting the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating that an oversized block can bypass the size check or that the check occurs after costly processing.

properties.text: For all valid blocks in post-merge Ethereum, block.ommers MUST equal the empty tuple (). Any block with non-empty ommers MUST be rejected as InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer can include non-empty ommers to trigger pre-merge code paths.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting non-empty ommers post-merge could trigger unexpected pre-merge processing logic, potentially causing consensus divergence between clients.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating that non-empty ommers bypass the check in a specific client implementation.

properties.text: For all valid blocks, the following 8 equalities MUST hold simultaneously: (1) block_output.block_gas_used == block.header.gas_used, (2) transactions_root == block.header.transactions_root, (3) state_root == block.header.state_root, (4) receipt_root == block.header.receipt_root, (5) block_logs_bloom == block.header.bloom, (6) withdrawals_root == block.header.withdrawals_root, (7) block_output.blob_gas_used == block.header.blob_gas_used, (8) requests_hash == block.header.requests_hash. Failure of any single comparison MUST cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: An attacker proposes a block with carefully crafted header fields that differ from computed values. If any comparison can be bypassed, an invalid state transition is accepted.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing any root/hash comparison allows committing an invalid state transition, leading to consensus failure across the network and potential fund loss.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Any inconsistency in root/hash verification that allows an invalid block to be accepted constitutes a critical consensus vulnerability.

properties.text: After appending a new block, the chain MUST retain at most 255 blocks. If chain.blocks length exceeds 255, blocks MUST be pruned from the beginning to maintain this bound.

reachability.notes: Pruning is an internal operation triggered after every block append. No external input can directly control the pruning behavior.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to prune causes unbounded memory growth over time but does not directly affect consensus or security.

properties.text: The base fee increase delta MUST be at least 1 when parent_gas_used > parent_gas_target. Formally: if parent_gas_used > parent_gas_limit // ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER, then base_fee_per_gas_delta >= 1.

reachability.notes: Proposers control gas_limit and indirectly influence gas_used. The minimum increment of 1 prevents base fee stagnation.

properties.severity_justification: The asymmetric base fee adjustment is by design. Exploitation requires sustained proposer control and has limited impact due to economic incentives.

properties.text: The base fee per gas MUST NOT increase by more than parent_base_fee_per_gas * parent_gas_used_delta / (parent_gas_target * BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR) per block, with a minimum increase of 1. Formally: base_fee_per_gas_delta <= max(parent_base_fee * gas_delta / (target * DENOMINATOR), 1).

reachability.notes: A proposer sets gas_limit which influences base fee calculation. Incorrect base fee calculation could cause consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect base fee calculation causes blocks to be validated differently across clients, leading to consensus splits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that a specific gas_limit/gas_used combination produces different base fees in different client implementations.

properties.text: The gas target MUST equal parent_gas_limit // ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER where ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER == 2. Any deviation from this calculation MUST cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Purely internal calculation constant. Not directly controllable by external actors.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect elasticity multiplier could cause base fee miscalculation, leading to consensus issues across clients.

properties.text: The gas limit MUST pass check_gas_limit validation. Specifically: (1) gas_limit < parent_gas_limit + parent_gas_limit // 1024, (2) gas_limit > parent_gas_limit - parent_gas_limit // 1024, (3) gas_limit >= GAS_LIMIT_MINIMUM (5000). All three conditions MUST hold.

reachability.notes: A proposer sets the gas_limit field. The adjustment is bounded to ~0.1% per block, but a colluding set of proposers could drift it over many blocks.

properties.severity_justification: Requires sustained control of block production to drift gas limit to extreme values. Economic incentives and validator rotation mitigate this.

properties.text: Block number MUST be >= 1. Any block with header.number < 1 MUST be rejected as InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer could set block number to 0 to trigger edge cases in parent lookup.

properties.severity_justification: Block number 0 or negative could cause index-out-of-bounds in chain.blocks[-1] lookup, potentially crashing the node.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that block number 0 causes crash or unexpected behavior in a client.

properties.text: Block timestamps MUST be strictly increasing. For all valid blocks: header.timestamp > parent_header.timestamp. A block with header.timestamp <= parent_header.timestamp MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: A proposer can set the timestamp field. Non-strictly-increasing timestamps could break time-dependent logic.

properties.severity_justification: Allowing equal or decreasing timestamps could affect time-dependent calculations (e.g., difficulty adjustment, slot timing) and cause consensus splits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a client accepting a block with timestamp <= parent timestamp.

properties.text: Block numbers MUST be sequential. For all valid blocks: header.number == parent_header.number + 1. Any gap or skip in block numbers MUST cause rejection.

reachability.notes: A proposer can set an arbitrary block number. Skipping block numbers could cause chain history inconsistencies.

properties.severity_justification: Non-sequential block numbers would corrupt chain state and break the block hash history used by get_last_256_block_hashes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate chain corruption from non-sequential block numbers in a client.

properties.text: Block extra_data MUST NOT exceed 32 bytes. For all valid blocks: len(header.extra_data) <= 32. Blocks with extra_data longer than 32 bytes MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: A proposer controls the extra_data field. Oversized extra_data increases block size but is bounded by this check.

properties.severity_justification: Extra data beyond 32 bytes has limited security impact but could affect block serialization consistency.

properties.text: In post-merge Ethereum, header.difficulty MUST equal 0. Any block with difficulty != 0 MUST be rejected as InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: A proposer can set difficulty to non-zero to attempt to trigger pre-merge code paths.

properties.severity_justification: Non-zero difficulty post-merge could trigger PoW-related code paths in clients that still retain them, causing divergent behavior.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a client processing a non-zero difficulty block post-merge.

properties.text: In post-merge Ethereum, header.nonce MUST equal 0x0000000000000000. Any block with nonce != 0 MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: A proposer controls the nonce field. Non-zero nonce could trigger PoW verification code paths.

properties.severity_justification: Non-zero nonce post-merge could cause consensus divergence if clients handle it differently.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Show divergent client behavior on non-zero nonce post-merge.

properties.text: In post-merge Ethereum, header.ommers_hash MUST equal EMPTY_OMMER_HASH (keccak256 of RLP-encoded empty list). Any deviation MUST cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Double enforcement with PROP-0002 (ommers tuple check in state_transition). Provides defense-in-depth.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent ommers_hash could indicate a crafted block attempting to exploit pre-merge semantics.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate bypass of both ommers_hash and ommers tuple checks.

properties.text: The parent_hash in a block header MUST equal keccak256(rlp.encode(parent_header)). Any mismatch MUST cause block rejection as InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: This is a critical chain integrity check. Any bypass allows chain reorganization attacks by replacing parent blocks.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing parent hash verification allows chain reorganization, history rewriting, and potential double-spend attacks affecting the entire network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate any implementation bug in parent hash verification that allows block acceptance with incorrect parent.

properties.text: The excess_blob_gas in a block header MUST equal calculate_excess_blob_gas(parent_header). Any mismatch MUST cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Incorrect excess_blob_gas calculation could affect blob pricing. Edge cases in underflow (when target > actual) are relevant for EIP-7892 and EIP-7918.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect excess blob gas causes divergent blob fee calculations across clients, leading to consensus splits on blob transaction validity.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate edge case in excess blob gas calculation causing client divergence.

properties.text: For all valid blocks, header.gas_used MUST NOT exceed header.gas_limit. Formally: header.gas_used <= header.gas_limit.

reachability.notes: A proposer sets both gas_used and gas_limit. Setting gas_used > gas_limit would violate the gas accounting invariant.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting gas_used > gas_limit would indicate broken gas accounting, potentially allowing more computation than paid for.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a client accepting a block where gas_used exceeds gas_limit.

properties.text: Transaction gas MUST NOT exceed remaining block gas. For each transaction: tx.gas <= (block_gas_limit - block_gas_used). Violation MUST raise GasUsedExceedsLimitError.

reachability.notes: An attacker controls the gas field of their transaction. Bypassing this check would allow exceeding the block gas limit.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing the gas limit check allows transactions to consume more gas than the block permits, potentially causing unbounded computation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a transaction exceeding block gas limit being accepted.

properties.text: Transaction blob gas MUST NOT exceed remaining block blob gas. For blob transactions: calculate_total_blob_gas(tx) <= blob_gas_available. Violation MUST raise BlobGasLimitExceededError.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls blob count and hence blob gas. Bypassing this could allow exceeding the block blob gas limit.

properties.severity_justification: Exceeding blob gas limit affects data availability guarantees and could cause consensus splits if clients compute different blob gas totals.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate blob gas limit bypass with excess blobs being accepted.

properties.text: For EIP-1559 transactions (FeeMarket, Blob, SetCode types), max_fee_per_gas MUST be >= max_priority_fee_per_gas. Violation MUST raise PriorityFeeGreaterThanMaxFeeError.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls both fee fields. If priority > max, effective gas price calculation could overflow or produce unexpected results.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing this check could cause integer overflow in effective gas price calculation in fixed-width integer implementations (Go/Rust/Java).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate integer overflow in effective gas price due to priority > max fee in a specific client.

properties.text: For all EIP-1559 transactions, max_fee_per_gas MUST be >= base_fee_per_gas. Violation MUST raise InsufficientMaxFeePerGasError.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls max_fee_per_gas. Accepting transactions with insufficient fees would allow underpaying for computation.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting underpaying transactions breaks the fee market mechanism but requires block proposer collusion to include them.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a transaction accepted with max_fee < base_fee in a client.

properties.text: Blob transactions MUST have between 1 and MAX_BLOB_COUNT (inclusive) blobs. Formally: 1 <= len(tx.blob_versioned_hashes) <= MAX_BLOB_COUNT. Empty blob list MUST raise NoBlobDataError; exceeding limit MUST raise BlobCountExceededError.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls the number of blob versioned hashes in a transaction. Exceeding MAX_BLOB_COUNT could cause excessive data availability processing.

properties.severity_justification: Exceeding MAX_BLOB_COUNT could overwhelm data availability sampling and CL processing, affecting network-wide data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate acceptance of a blob transaction with more than MAX_BLOB_COUNT blobs.

properties.text: ALL blob versioned hashes MUST have version prefix equal to VERSIONED_HASH_VERSION_KZG (0x01). For every hash in tx.blob_versioned_hashes: hash[0] == 0x01. Any invalid version MUST raise InvalidBlobVersionedHashError.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls blob versioned hashes. Accepting non-KZG version prefixes could allow uncommitted blob data.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blobs with wrong version prefix could compromise data availability guarantees, as KZG proofs would not be verified for non-KZG versions.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate acceptance of a blob with version prefix != 0x01.

properties.text: Blob and SetCode transactions MUST NOT create contracts. For BlobTransaction and SetCodeTransaction types: tx.to MUST be an Address (not None). Violation MUST raise TransactionTypeContractCreationError.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls the 'to' field. Allowing contract creation via blob/setcode transactions could enable unexpected behavior.

properties.severity_justification: Contract creation via these transaction types is undefined behavior and could lead to consensus divergence between clients that handle it differently.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate contract creation via blob or setcode transaction being accepted.

properties.text: SetCode transactions MUST have a non-empty authorization list. For SetCodeTransaction: len(tx.authorization_list) > 0 AND any(tx.authorization_list) == True. Violation MUST raise EmptyAuthorizationListError.

reachability.notes: Attacker crafts SetCode transactions. Empty authorization list bypasses the delegation mechanism.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing EIP-7702 authorization list validation could allow unauthorized code delegation, enabling attackers to gain execution authority over accounts they do not control.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate unauthorized code delegation via SetCode transaction with bypassed authorization check.

properties.text: Sender nonce MUST match transaction nonce exactly. For all transactions: sender_account.nonce == tx.nonce. Sender nonce > tx.nonce MUST raise NonceMismatchError (nonce too low). Sender nonce < tx.nonce MUST raise NonceMismatchError (nonce too high).

reachability.notes: Attacker controls the nonce field. Bypassing nonce check enables replay attacks or nonce skipping.

properties.severity_justification: Nonce bypass enables transaction replay, allowing the same transaction to be executed multiple times, causing double-spending.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate nonce check bypass allowing transaction replay.

properties.text: Sender balance MUST be sufficient to cover maximum gas fee plus transaction value. Formally: sender.balance >= (tx.gas * tx.max_fee_per_gas) + tx.value [+ blob_gas_fee for blob txs]. Violation MUST raise InsufficientBalanceError.

reachability.notes: An attacker with insufficient balance attempts to execute transactions. Bypassing the balance check enables spending beyond available funds.

properties.severity_justification: Balance check bypass allows spending ETH without having it, directly causing fund loss for other parties.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate fund spending beyond account balance.

properties.text: A sender account with deployed code MUST have a valid delegation designation to send transactions. If sender has code AND the code does not begin with the EIP-7702 delegation prefix, the transaction MUST be rejected with InvalidSenderError.

reachability.notes: An attacker could attempt to send transactions from a contract account without proper delegation. Bypassing this check enables unauthorized transaction initiation from smart contracts.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing sender code check allows arbitrary contracts to initiate transactions, breaking the EOA-only transaction origin model and enabling privilege escalation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate unauthorized transaction from a contract account without valid delegation.

properties.text: The gas refund for any transaction MUST NOT exceed gas_used // 5 (EIP-3529 cap). Formally: tx_gas_refund = min(gas_used // 5, tx_output.refund_counter).

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts transactions to maximize the refund counter. If the cap is not enforced, excess gas is refunded, creating an economic exploit.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect refund cap allows transactions to receive more gas back than intended, enabling below-cost execution and potential DoS via gas market manipulation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a transaction receiving refund exceeding gas_used // 5.

properties.text: After gas refund application, the effective gas used MUST be at least the calldata floor gas cost (EIP-7623). Formally: tx_gas_used = max(gas_used - refund, calldata_floor_gas_cost). The calldata floor MUST be enforced AFTER the refund cap.

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts transactions with large calldata and high refund to pay less than the calldata floor. The ordering of refund then floor is critical.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing the calldata floor allows cheap data stuffing attacks, undermining the economic protections introduced by EIP-7623 for Fusaka.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a transaction paying less than the calldata floor gas cost.

properties.text: The sender MUST pay effective_gas_fee + blob_gas_fee upfront before message execution. Formally: sender_balance_before_execution = sender_balance - (tx.gas * effective_gas_price) - blob_gas_fee. This deduction MUST occur BEFORE the EVM message call.

reachability.notes: If fee deduction happens after execution, the sender could spend the fee budget during execution and then fail to pay fees.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect ordering allows sender to use fee budget during execution, obtaining free computation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate fee deduction ordering bug allowing free computation.

properties.text: Unused gas MUST be refunded to the sender at the effective_gas_price. Formally: gas_left = tx.gas - tx_gas_used; sender_balance += gas_left * effective_gas_price.

reachability.notes: Incorrect gas refund calculation could result in sender losing funds or receiving excess funds.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect gas refund affects individual transaction economics but is bounded by the transaction gas limit.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate incorrect gas refund calculation.

properties.text: The coinbase (block proposer) MUST receive only the priority fee portion of the gas price. Formally: coinbase_payment = tx_gas_used * (effective_gas_price - base_fee_per_gas). The base fee portion MUST be burned (not paid to anyone).

reachability.notes: If coinbase receives the full gas price instead of just the priority fee, the EIP-1559 burn mechanism is broken, causing ETH supply inflation.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect coinbase payment breaks EIP-1559 fee burning, affecting ETH monetary policy at a protocol level.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate coinbase receiving full gas price instead of priority fee only.

properties.text: The sender's nonce MUST be incremented BEFORE EVM message execution. Formally: increment_nonce(state, sender) is called before process_message_call(message).

reachability.notes: If nonce increment is deferred until after execution, the sender could exploit reentrancy to submit multiple transactions with the same nonce during execution.

properties.severity_justification: Nonce increment after execution enables reentrancy-based nonce reuse, allowing multiple transactions with the same nonce in a single block.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate nonce reuse via reentrancy when nonce is incremented after execution.

properties.text: All accounts marked for deletion (selfdestruct) MUST be destroyed AFTER transaction execution completes. The accounts_to_delete set from the execution output MUST be processed deterministically.

reachability.notes: An attacker can trigger selfdestruct via crafted transactions. Non-deterministic deletion ordering could cause consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic account deletion ordering causes state divergence between clients, leading to consensus splits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate divergent selfdestruct behavior across clients.

properties.text: System transactions MUST always originate from SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe). No other address MUST be able to impersonate the system address for system transactions.

reachability.notes: SYSTEM_ADDRESS is hardcoded. An attacker cannot directly call system transactions, but a bug in the dispatch could allow non-system addresses to trigger system contract calls.

properties.severity_justification: Impersonating SYSTEM_ADDRESS allows unauthorized system contract interactions, potentially manipulating beacon roots, history storage, or withdrawal/consolidation requests.

properties.text: System transactions MUST use exactly SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS (30,000,000) gas. The gas amount MUST NOT be configurable or variable.

reachability.notes: Gas is a hardcoded constant for system transactions. No external input controls it.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect gas constant could cause system transactions to fail if too low or waste gas if too high, but is unlikely to be a security issue.

properties.text: System transactions MUST NOT transfer value. Both should_transfer_value MUST be False and value MUST be 0. No ETH MUST be moved by system transactions themselves.

reachability.notes: System transactions with value transfer could drain the SYSTEM_ADDRESS balance or credit system contracts with unauthorized ETH.

properties.severity_justification: Value transfer in system transactions would create or destroy ETH, affecting the monetary supply integrity.

properties.text: For checked system transactions, the target contract MUST contain code (len(code) > 0). If the contract has no code, the block MUST be rejected as InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: If system contracts are not properly deployed at fork activation, any block would be rejected, halting the chain. An attacker cannot directly control system contract code, but state corruption could remove it.

properties.severity_justification: Missing system contract code causes all blocks to be invalid, completely halting the Ethereum chain.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a scenario where system contract code is missing or removed, causing chain halt.

properties.text: For checked system transactions, the execution MUST succeed (error is None). If the system transaction produces an error, the block MUST be rejected as InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: An attacker who can cause the system contract to revert (e.g., by manipulating contract state via user transactions) could prevent valid blocks from being produced, halting the chain.

properties.severity_justification: Causing system contract revert makes all blocks invalid, halting the entire Ethereum network. This is a chain-stopping vulnerability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a user transaction that corrupts system contract state, causing subsequent system transactions to revert and halting the chain.

properties.text: Unchecked system transactions (beacon roots, history storage) MUST NOT validate contract code existence or execution success. The process_unchecked_system_transaction function MUST silently proceed regardless of the target contract state.

reachability.notes: The unchecked nature means beacon roots and history storage system transactions always succeed. If a client incorrectly adds checks, valid blocks would be rejected.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect validation of unchecked system transactions could cause valid blocks to be rejected, leading to consensus divergence.

properties.text: In the block body execution order: (1) beacon roots system transaction MUST execute first, (2) history storage system transaction MUST execute second, (3) user transactions MUST execute in order after system transactions, (4) withdrawals MUST process after all transactions, (5) general purpose requests MUST process last.

reachability.notes: The execution order is deterministic and protocol-defined. Any client that reorders these operations will produce a different state root, causing consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect execution ordering causes different state roots across clients, leading to network-wide consensus failure.

properties.text: General purpose requests MUST be assembled in ascending order of request type: deposits (DEPOSIT_REQUEST_TYPE), then withdrawals (WITHDRAWAL_REQUEST_TYPE), then consolidations (CONSOLIDATION_REQUEST_TYPE). This ordering MUST be deterministic.

reachability.notes: Request ordering affects the requests_hash in the block header. An attacker cannot control the ordering directly, but deposit requests come from transaction logs which are attacker-influenced.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect request ordering produces different requests_hash, causing blocks to be rejected or accepted inconsistently across clients.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate request ordering inconsistency causing consensus divergence.

properties.text: Deposit requests MUST be parsed from block output logs (not from system transactions). The parse_deposit_requests function MUST correctly parse log entries emitted during block execution.

reachability.notes: An attacker can emit arbitrary logs via crafted transactions. If the deposit log parser accepts logs from the wrong address or with incorrect ABI decoding, fraudulent deposit requests could be injected.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect deposit log parsing could inject fraudulent deposits, corrupting the beacon chain deposit queue and validator set.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate fraudulent deposit injection via crafted log emissions.

properties.text: Withdrawal and consolidation requests MUST come from checked system transactions that MUST succeed. If either system transaction fails, the block MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: This is a cross-reference with PROP-0041. System transaction failure causes chain halt.

properties.severity_justification: Failure of withdrawal or consolidation system transactions halts the chain by making all blocks invalid.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Same as PROP-0041 -- demonstrate system contract revert causing chain halt.

properties.text: Withdrawal amounts MUST be scaled by 10^9 (Gwei to Wei conversion). The balance increase for each withdrawal MUST equal withdrawal.amount * 10^9. An incorrect scaling factor MUST NOT be used.

reachability.notes: The scaling factor is a protocol constant. An incorrect implementation (e.g., using 10^8 or 10^10) would inflate or deflate withdrawal amounts.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect Gwei-to-Wei conversion creates or destroys ETH, directly affecting the monetary supply of the entire network.

properties.text: Withdrawal processing MUST only increase account balances, never decrease them. For all withdrawals: the modify_state operation on the withdrawal address MUST add the scaled amount to the existing balance.

reachability.notes: A bug that decreases balance during withdrawal processing would cause validator fund loss.

properties.severity_justification: Decreasing balance during withdrawal is a direct fund loss vulnerability affecting all validators who withdraw.

properties.text: Transaction signatures MUST be unforgeable. The recover_sender function MUST correctly derive the sender address from the ECDSA signature (v, r, s) over the transaction hash. Malleable signatures (high-s values) MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit transactions with forged or malleable signatures. If recover_sender has edge-case bugs, the attacker could impersonate another account.

properties.severity_justification: Signature forgery allows impersonation of any account, enabling arbitrary fund theft and complete account takeover.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate signature malleability or forgery that allows sender impersonation.

properties.text: RLP encoding and decoding MUST be deterministic and collision-free. The same block/transaction MUST always produce the same RLP encoding, and different blocks/transactions MUST produce different RLP encodings.

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic RLP encoding would cause different clients to compute different block hashes, state roots, and transaction hashes, resulting in consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic RLP encoding causes immediate consensus failure across the entire network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate an input that produces different RLP encodings in different client implementations.

properties.text: Keccak256 hash function MUST be collision-resistant. All block hash, state root, transaction root, and receipt root computations depend on keccak256 providing 256-bit collision resistance.

reachability.notes: While keccak256 collision is computationally infeasible, implementation bugs in the hash function or comparison logic could be exploited.

properties.severity_justification: Hash collision or comparison bypass allows block forgery, chain reorganization, and complete consensus failure.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a keccak256 implementation bug that produces incorrect hashes.

properties.text: get_last_256_block_hashes MUST return at most 256 hashes, in order of increasing block number, with only the most recent hash computed via keccak256 and all others using parent_hash from successor blocks.

reachability.notes: Purely internal function. Hash list is consumed by the BLOCKHASH opcode.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect block hash list affects BLOCKHASH opcode but has limited direct security impact.

properties.text: apply_fork for the Osaka fork MUST be an identity transformation (no irregular state change). The function MUST return the state unchanged.

reachability.notes: Fork activation function. If it modifies state unexpectedly, it would cause immediate consensus failure at fork transition.

properties.severity_justification: Unexpected state modification at fork activation causes consensus failure at the exact fork block.

properties.text: Transaction validation checks MUST be ordered from general to specific: type check, then fee checks, then gas checks, then blob-specific checks, then authorization checks. All error paths MUST terminate by raising an InvalidTransaction subclass.

reachability.notes: Reordering validation checks could allow attackers to waste CPU on expensive late checks. However, this is a low-effort DoS which may be out of scope.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect validation ordering is primarily a DoS vector through wasted computation, but the impact is limited.

properties.text: Blob transaction validation MUST check data presence before count validation, gas limit before fee sufficiency, and MUST fail on the first invalid versioned hash (short-circuit evaluation).

reachability.notes: Attacker controls blob transaction parameters. Incorrect validation ordering could accept invalid blob transactions.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect blob validation ordering could allow edge-case invalid blob transactions to pass, affecting data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate an invalid blob transaction being accepted due to incorrect validation ordering.

properties.text: Receipt succeeded field MUST be True if and only if the transaction execution error is None. Formally: receipt.succeeded == (error is None). The receipt bloom MUST be computed from logs via logs_bloom.

reachability.notes: Incorrect receipt generation affects the receipt root, causing block validation failure. A subtle mismatch could cause consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect receipt generation causes receipt root mismatch, leading to consensus divergence between clients.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate receipt generation inconsistency causing root mismatch.

properties.text: The Engine API MUST be JWT-authenticated and MUST NOT be exposed to untrusted networks. All CL-to-EL communication MUST traverse the authenticated Engine API boundary.

reachability.notes: Engine API exposure is a configuration/deployment issue, explicitly out of scope for the bug bounty program.

properties.severity_justification: Exposed Engine API allows injection of malicious block parameters, withdrawals, and beacon roots.

properties.text: Exception classes storing transaction data (TransactionTypeContractCreationError, etc.) MUST NOT expose full transaction details in error messages surfaced to external callers.

reachability.notes: Information disclosure via error messages is only exploitable via JSON-RPC, which is explicitly out of scope.

properties.severity_justification: Transaction data in error messages is only observable via out-of-scope APIs.

properties.text: For blocks received via P2P that are just under MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE but contain maximally complex transactions, the validation MUST complete without excessive resource consumption. The validation order (size check first, then header, then execution) MUST minimize wasted work on invalid blocks.

reachability.notes: An attacker sends blocks designed to maximize processing time while staying under the size limit. This tests the bounds of acceptable processing cost.

properties.severity_justification: Resource exhaustion from near-limit-sized complex blocks could slow validator processing but is bounded by gas limits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate disproportionate resource consumption from a block just under the size limit.

properties.text: A compromised CL sending incorrect parent_beacon_block_root via Engine API MUST NOT corrupt the beacon roots ring buffer in a way that is detectable by EL-side validation. The unchecked nature of this system transaction means the EL trusts the CL input unconditionally.

reachability.notes: Requires compromised CL. The EL performs no validation on beacon root correctness, relying entirely on CL integrity.

properties.severity_justification: Corrupted beacon roots affect smart contracts relying on EIP-4788, but require CL compromise which has independent security guarantees.

properties.text: Fee-related exception objects (InsufficientMaxFeePerGasError) MUST store both transaction_max_fee_per_gas and block_base_fee_per_gas as Final[Uint] (immutable) fields. These fields MUST accurately reflect the values that caused the validation failure.

reachability.notes: Internal error object construction. Correctness matters for debugging but has no direct security impact.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect exception field values affect debugging and error reporting but have no direct security impact.

properties.text: For all EIP-1559 fee calculations involving near-uint256-boundary values (max_fee_per_gas, max_priority_fee_per_gas near 2^256-1), the effective_gas_fee computation (tx.gas * effective_gas_price) MUST NOT overflow in fixed-width integer implementations. Client implementations in Go/Rust/Java MUST handle these edge cases without overflow.

reachability.notes: Python specs use arbitrary-precision integers, but client implementations may use fixed-width. An attacker can submit transactions with extreme fee values to trigger overflow.

properties.severity_justification: Integer overflow in fee calculation could cause incorrect balance deductions, fee-free execution, or client crashes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate integer overflow in fee calculation in a specific client implementation.

properties.text: The consensus layer MUST provide correct and timely withdrawal information. Withdrawals directly increase account balances without EL-side validity verification. The EL trusts the CL to only include valid, authorized withdrawals.

reachability.notes: A compromised or buggy CL could inject fraudulent withdrawals, creating ETH from nothing. The EL has no mechanism to validate withdrawal legitimacy.

properties.severity_justification: Fraudulent withdrawals create ETH from nothing, directly violating monetary supply integrity.

properties.text: Python f-string formatting of exception messages with user-controlled values (transaction_type, type names, fee values) MUST NOT be translatable to format string injection vulnerabilities in client implementations using other languages (Go fmt.Sprintf, Java String.format, Rust format!).

reachability.notes: Attacker controls transaction_type and fee values. If a client uses these as format specifiers rather than arguments, injection is possible.

properties.severity_justification: Format string injection is limited by the types involved (integers, type names) and requires a specific client implementation vulnerability.

properties.text: For blob transactions, the max_fee_per_blob_gas MUST be >= the current blob gas price (derived from excess_blob_gas). Violation MUST raise InsufficientMaxFeePerBlobGasError. This ensures economic viability of blob data submission.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls max_fee_per_blob_gas. Accepting underpaying blob transactions undermines the blob fee market.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blob transactions with insufficient fees breaks the blob fee market mechanism but requires proposer collusion.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate blob transaction accepted with fee below blob gas price.
